title: Japan records five consecutive days of extreme temperatures, the longest streak in history
summary: Temperatures exceeded 40°C in several locations in Gifu and Mie prefectures, and at least one heatstroke death was reported.

title: JungleRia theme park in Okinawa celebrates its first year with one million visitors and economic impact of 49.4 billion yen
summary: Although it surpassed the attendance target, management recognizes challenges in operations and seeks to improve the experience to sustain growth.

title: Shigeki Inaba takes over as new manager of Japan's national baseball team (Samurai Japan)
summary: Inaba, the first manager with Major League experience, plans to merge Japanese tradition with physical strength to conquer the world.

title: 10 years after the Sagamihara disability center massacre, ceremonies are held in memory of the victims
summary: Commemorative events, including statements from the incarcerated perpetrator, underscore the need to eradicate discrimination and abuse against people with disabilities.

title: India's Education Minister resigns amid massive protests over university exam fraud scandal
summary: The protests, driven by the 'Cockroaches of the People' party, forced the official's resignation after corruption in the admissions system was uncovered.

title: Aonishiki takes the lead in the Nagoya sumo tournament, followed by Kirishima and Atami Fuji
summary: With three wrestlers in contention, the title will be decided on the last day of the summer tournament.

title: The 'Kawahiki' ritual to transport wood to Ise Shrine begins in preparation for the 2033 renovation
summary: More than 3,600 people participated in the dragging of logs along the river, marking the start of preparations for the periodic reconstruction of the Shinto shrine.

title: US and South Korean companies agree on massive semiconductor cooperation for artificial intelligence
summary: The alliance, mobilizing between 110 and 155 trillion yen, aims to strengthen the AI chip supply chain and global competitiveness.

title: Ishin party proposes holding the referendum on the Osaka Metropolis alongside the unified local elections
summary: The initiative has been criticized by the opposition, which sees it as a maneuver to concentrate power and disregard parliamentary democracy.

title: Osaka, Fukuoka, and Nagoya compete to become Japan's 'subcapital' after the enactment of the new law
summary: The subcapital law aims to decentralize administrative functions from Tokyo, and several cities have shown interest in hosting the new seat.

title: Kozo Okamoto, former member of the Japanese Red Army, dies in Lebanon at age 77
summary: Okamoto, who participated in the 1972 Lod Airport massacre, died of pulmonary complications; his funeral was attended by leaders of the Palestinian organization PFLP.

title: Yokozuna Hoshoryu withdraws from the Nagoya sumo tournament due to a right leg injury
summary: After suffering six defeats due to his physical condition, the wrestler decided to withdraw from the competition and will undergo six weeks of treatment.

title: Electric saw sold on an auction site linked to murder and dismemberment case in Tone River
summary: The victim's DNA was found on the tool, which was sold after the crime, leading police to investigate the seller.

title: Trump hosts dinner for journalists, repeats personal attacks and suggests running for a third term
summary: The event, rescheduled after an assassination attempt, created a tense atmosphere as Trump criticized several attendees and media outlets.

title: Okamoto Kazuma breaks Ohtani's record for most home runs by a Japanese rookie in Major League Baseball
summary: The Tokyo Giants batter hit his twenty-third home run of the season, setting a new record for Japanese players in their debut year.

title: Seven & i Holdings abandons investment plan in convenience store chain in Poland
summary: The Japanese company failed to reach an agreement on financial terms with the local partner and is reconsidering its global expansion strategy.

title: Various high school baseball teams secure their spots in the National Summer Koshien Tournament
summary: Hanamaki Higashi, Higashinihon Kokusai Daisho, and other schools won regional finals and qualified for the prestigious summer tournament.
